discovery_method: deterministic utility-library sweep (Python/JS/Rust pure libraries verified via PyPI/npm/crates.io/GitHub fetch; inherently deterministic capabilities — the easiest negative-space targets to distill to deterministic rules)
governance: CANDIDATES ONLY — discovery is not trust.

candidates.intent: Parse a date/time string in almost any common format into a normalized datetime, handling 2- vs 4-digit years, ambiguous day/month order, and embedded timezones.
candidates.input_contract: a date/time string plus optional dayfirst/yearfirst hints
candidates.output_contract: a timezone-aware datetime object (or a structured parse error)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM parsing dates by reasoning is non-deterministic across runs, silently mis-orders ambiguous DD/MM dates, and cannot guarantee a valid datetime — wasting tokens on a solved parsing problem.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Battle-tested grammar-based parser handles thousands of format permutations deterministically with explicit dayfirst/yearfirst control and reproducible output every time.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/dateutil/dateutil, PyPI python-dateutil, dual Apache-2.0/BSD per repo. Pure deterministic parser; residual is genuinely ambiguous human strings.

candidates.intent: Expand an iCalendar RRULE recurrence specification into the concrete list of occurrence datetimes (e.g. 'every 2nd Tuesday', 'last weekday of the month').
candidates.input_contract: an RRULE string or recurrence parameters plus a start datetime and a window
candidates.output_contract: an ordered list of occurrence datetimes within the window
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot reliably enumerate every occurrence of a complex recurrence rule over a long window — it drops or invents dates, and the result is non-reproducible.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Implements the full iCalendar RFC 5545 recurrence algebra deterministically; every occurrence is computed exactly and identically across runs.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: dateutil.rrule implements RFC 5545 recurrence. Fully deterministic enumeration.

candidates.intent: Parse, shift, format, and humanize datetimes (e.g. 'in 2 hours', '3 days ago') with timezone awareness and locale support.
candidates.input_contract: a datetime, timestamp, or ISO string plus optional timezone/locale
candidates.output_contract: a normalized Arrow datetime and/or a humanized relative string
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Asking an LLM to format relative times or shift across DST/timezones gives inconsistent phrasing and arithmetic errors at DST boundaries.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Provides a deterministic, DST-correct datetime engine with locale-aware humanization, identical for the same inputs.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/arrow-py/arrow (arrow-py org), PyPI 'arrow', Apache-2.0. Distinct from apache/arrow (columnar format).

candidates.intent: Perform timezone- and DST-aware datetime arithmetic, differences, and period iteration as a drop-in datetime replacement.
candidates.input_contract: datetimes/durations plus an IANA timezone
candidates.output_contract: DST-correct datetimes, durations, and periods
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs routinely botch DST transitions, leap handling, and timezone math, producing off-by-one-hour answers that are unsafe for scheduling.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic, DST-aware datetime library that inherits from stdlib datetime; arithmetic is exact and reproducible.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/python-pendulum/pendulum, PyPI 'pendulum', MIT. Fully deterministic.

candidates.intent: Parse human-readable and relative dates in many languages (e.g. '2 weeks ago', 'hace 3 dias') into datetimes.
candidates.input_contract: a free-text date string plus optional language/settings
candidates.output_contract: a parsed datetime or None
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM's multilingual date parsing is plausible-but-wrong on edge cases and not reproducible; it cannot guarantee a valid datetime.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Curated language data + deterministic rules parse 200+ locales' date expressions reproducibly, with the residual returned as None rather than hallucinated.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/scrapinghub/dateparser, BSD-3. Mostly deterministic; a small heuristic residual on truly ambiguous multilingual text keeps the ceiling just under 1.0.

candidates.intent: Convert and arithmetically combine physical quantities across units (length, mass, temperature, energy, etc.) with dimensional-consistency checking.
candidates.input_contract: a magnitude + source unit and a target unit (or a quantity expression)
candidates.output_contract: the converted magnitude in the target unit, or a dimensionality error
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs make arithmetic and conversion-factor errors (especially affine units like temperature) and won't catch dimensionally invalid operations — a known hallucination source.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A unit registry enforces dimensional consistency and applies exact conversion factors deterministically, rejecting invalid operations instead of guessing.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/hgrecco/pint, PyPI 'Pint', BSD-3. Fully deterministic unit algebra.

candidates.intent: Parse, validate, and format an international phone number, returning region, type, and E.164/national formatting.
candidates.input_contract: a phone-number string plus an optional default region
candidates.output_contract: validity, region, number type, and E.164/national/international formats
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot reliably know per-country numbering plans, valid lengths, and carrier rules; it formats inconsistently and accepts invalid numbers.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A Python port of Google's libphonenumber metadata applies exact per-region numbering rules deterministically for validation and canonical formatting.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/daviddrysdale/python-phonenumbers (port of Google libphonenumber), Apache-2.0. Deterministic, metadata-driven.

candidates.intent: Validate the syntax of an email address (incl. internationalized addresses), normalize it, and optionally check domain deliverability.
candidates.input_contract: an email-address string plus options (allow IDN, check deliverability)
candidates.output_contract: a normalized address with local/domain parts, or a structured validation error
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs accept malformed addresses and apply inconsistent normalization; email RFC syntax + IDN rules are precise and not a reasoning task.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Implements RFC 5321/5322 + IDNA syntax rules deterministically and returns a canonical normalized form.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/JoshData/python-email-validator, Unlicense per repo. Syntax+normalization is deterministic; the optional DNS deliverability check is the only network-dependent part.

candidates.intent: Validate common data values — URLs, emails, IP addresses, MAC addresses, IBANs, UUIDs, domains, slugs, card numbers — with a uniform API.
candidates.input_contract: a value plus the validator type to apply
candidates.output_contract: a boolean/validation result (True or a ValidationError)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Asking an LLM 'is this a valid IBAN/MAC/URL' yields inconsistent yes/no answers and misses checksum/format rules.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Encodes the exact format and checksum rules for each value type as deterministic validators.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/python-validators/validators, PyPI 'validators', MIT. Deterministic format validators.

candidates.intent: Convert an arbitrary Unicode string into a clean, URL-safe ASCII slug with transliteration and configurable separators.
candidates.input_contract: a Unicode string plus options (max length, separator, stopwords)
candidates.output_contract: a deterministic ASCII slug string
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLM slugification varies run-to-run and handles Unicode transliteration inconsistently, breaking URL stability.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic transliteration + normalization produces a stable, idempotent slug for the same input every time.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/un33k/python-slugify, PyPI 'python-slugify', MIT. Fully deterministic.

candidates.intent: Accurately split a URL/hostname into subdomain, registered domain, and public suffix using the Public Suffix List.
candidates.input_contract: a URL or hostname string
candidates.output_contract: subdomain, domain, and suffix components
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Naive splitting on dots (and LLM guessing) fails on multi-level public suffixes like co.uk or s3.amazonaws.com; the LLM has no current PSL.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Uses the actual Public Suffix List to deterministically and correctly decompose any hostname.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/john-kurkowski/tldextract, BSD-3. Deterministic given a pinned PSL snapshot.

candidates.intent: Parse, modify, and re-serialize URLs and query strings (add/remove params, change path segments) safely.
candidates.input_contract: a URL string plus component mutations
candidates.output_contract: a correctly re-encoded URL string
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs mishandle URL percent-encoding and query-parameter ordering/escaping, producing malformed URLs.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic URL object model handles encoding, query manipulation, and re-serialization correctly.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/gruns/furl, PyPI 'furl', Unlicense. Deterministic URL manipulation.

candidates.intent: Validate a JSON/dict document against a JSON Schema (Draft 4-2020-12) and report precise validation errors with paths.
candidates.input_contract: a JSON instance plus a JSON Schema document
candidates.output_contract: valid/invalid plus a list of errors with JSON paths
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM asked to validate against a schema misses constraints (formats, conditionals, refs) and won't give exact error paths reproducibly.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Implements the JSON Schema spec deterministically, returning every violation with an exact instance path.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/python-jsonschema/jsonschema, PyPI 'jsonschema', MIT. Spec-conformant deterministic validator.

candidates.intent: Safely parse YAML into Python data structures and serialize Python data back to YAML.
candidates.input_contract: a YAML string (parse) or a Python object (emit)
candidates.output_contract: a Python object (parse) or a YAML string (emit)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs cannot losslessly round-trip YAML's full grammar (anchors, tags, multiline) and silently corrupt structure.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A spec-compliant YAML 1.1 parser/emitter handles the full grammar deterministically with safe_load for untrusted input.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/yaml/pyyaml, PyPI 'PyYAML', MIT. Deterministic parse/emit.

candidates.intent: Parse and re-emit YAML while preserving comments, key order, and formatting (round-trip mode).
candidates.input_contract: a YAML string with comments/formatting plus targeted edits
candidates.output_contract: modified YAML preserving original comments and layout
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM editing a YAML config destroys comments, reorders keys, and reformats unrelated sections.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Round-trip parser preserves comments/order so only the intended values change — deterministically.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: PyPI 'ruamel.yaml', MIT. Canonical home is the author's sourceforge; mirror at GitLab. Deterministic round-trip.

candidates.intent: Parse TOML configuration into Python data and serialize Python data to spec-compliant TOML.
candidates.input_contract: a TOML string (parse) or a Python object (emit)
candidates.output_contract: a Python dict (parse) or a TOML string (emit)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs produce subtly invalid TOML (quoting, datetime, array-of-tables) and cannot guarantee spec conformance.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A spec-compliant, style-preserving TOML parser/emitter handles the grammar deterministically.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/python-poetry/tomlkit, PyPI 'tomlkit', MIT. Style-preserving deterministic TOML.

candidates.intent: Parse and write delimited (CSV/TSV) data robustly, handling quoting, embedded newlines, and dialect detection.
candidates.input_contract: CSV text/stream plus a dialect (or sniff) — or rows to write
candidates.output_contract: parsed rows/records — or correctly quoted CSV text
candidates.gap_hypothesis: LLMs mangle quoted fields with commas/newlines and cannot guarantee RFC 4180-correct quoting on output.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A C-backed dialect-aware parser/writer handles quoting and escaping exactly per RFC 4180, reproducibly.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib csv module (Lib/csv.py), PSF License. Deterministic RFC 4180 handling.

candidates.intent: Compute cryptographic and message-digest hashes (SHA-256/512, SHA-3, BLAKE2, MD5) of bytes or streams.
candidates.input_contract: a byte string or file stream plus the algorithm name
candidates.output_contract: a hex/raw digest of the chosen algorithm
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM literally cannot compute a correct cryptographic digest — it is a precise bit-level function, not a reasoning task.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Standard, audited hash implementations produce exact, reproducible digests for content addressing and integrity.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib hashlib, PSF License. Bit-exact deterministic hashing.

candidates.intent: Hash a password with bcrypt (salted, work-factored) and verify a candidate password against a stored hash.
candidates.input_contract: a plaintext password (hash) or a password + stored hash (verify)
candidates.output_contract: a bcrypt hash string, or a boolean verification result
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot perform the bcrypt key-derivation function; password hashing is a precise, security-critical computation.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Audited bcrypt implementation produces correct salted hashes and constant-time verification deterministically.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/pyca/bcrypt, PyPI 'bcrypt', Apache-2.0. Verification is deterministic; hashing uses a random salt by design (still a correct primitive).

candidates.intent: Encode signed JSON Web Tokens and decode/verify them, checking signature, expiry, and claims.
candidates.input_contract: a claims payload + key/algorithm (encode) or a token + key (decode)
candidates.output_contract: a signed JWT string, or a verified claims payload / signature error
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot compute or verify HMAC/RSA signatures; JWT validation is a cryptographic, security-critical operation.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Implements RFC 7519 signing/verification with correct algorithm handling deterministically, rejecting tampered or expired tokens.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt, PyPI 'PyJWT', MIT. Deterministic verification.

candidates.intent: Encode and decode bytes to/from Base64, Base32, Base16, and URL-safe Base64.
candidates.input_contract: a byte string (encode) or an encoded string (decode) plus the variant
candidates.output_contract: the encoded string or the decoded bytes
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot reliably reproduce exact Base64 encoding/decoding of arbitrary bytes — it is a deterministic transform, not reasoning.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Standard codecs perform exact, reversible encoding/decoding for every byte sequence.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib base64, PSF License. Bit-exact deterministic.

candidates.intent: Generate UUIDs (v1/v3/v4/v5) and parse/validate/normalize UUID strings into canonical form.
candidates.input_contract: a UUID version + namespace/name (generate) or a UUID-ish string (parse)
candidates.output_contract: a canonical UUID (and its variant/version)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot generate spec-compliant UUIDs (correct version/variant bits) or deterministically derive v5 namespace UUIDs.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Standard UUID implementation sets version/variant bits correctly and derives namespaced UUIDs via exact hashing.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib uuid, PSF License. v3/v5 and parsing are deterministic; v4 is random by design.

candidates.intent: Create, read, append to, and extract ZIP archives with selectable compression.
candidates.input_contract: files/bytes to archive, or a ZIP archive to read/extract
candidates.output_contract: a ZIP archive, or extracted file entries
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Archive container formats are binary and exact; an LLM cannot produce or read a valid ZIP byte stream.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Standard library reads/writes spec-conformant ZIP containers deterministically.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib zipfile, PSF License. Deterministic container handling.

candidates.intent: Compress and decompress data using gzip/zlib (DEFLATE) with selectable levels.
candidates.input_contract: raw bytes (compress) or gzip bytes (decompress) plus a level
candidates.output_contract: compressed or decompressed bytes
candidates.gap_hypothesis: DEFLATE compression is a precise bit-level algorithm an LLM cannot execute.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Standard zlib bindings compress/decompress deterministically and losslessly.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib gzip/zlib, PSF License. Decompression is exact; compression output is deterministic per level/implementation.

candidates.intent: Open, resize, crop, rotate, convert format, and adjust images (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF/TIFF) programmatically.
candidates.input_contract: an image file/bytes plus transform parameters and a target format
candidates.output_contract: a transformed image in the requested format
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A text LLM cannot perform pixel-level image resizing/format conversion — it is binary image processing, not generation.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A mature imaging library performs exact, reproducible raster transforms and format conversions.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/python-pillow/Pillow, PyPI 'Pillow', HPND/MIT-CMU license. Deterministic for fixed resample filters.

candidates.intent: Extract EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata (camera, GPS, orientation, timestamp) from image files.
candidates.input_contract: an image file/bytes (JPEG/TIFF/HEIC)
candidates.output_contract: structured metadata tags incl. GPS coordinates
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Metadata lives in a binary container an LLM cannot parse; it would hallucinate fields rather than read them.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic EXIF parsing extracts the exact stored tags, including GPS, with no invention.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: Pillow ExifTags (github.com/python-pillow/Pillow). Deterministic tag extraction.

candidates.intent: Merge, split, reorder, rotate, crop, and extract pages from PDF files without rasterizing.
candidates.input_contract: one or more PDF files plus a page operation spec
candidates.output_contract: a new PDF with the requested page structure
candidates.gap_hypothesis: PDF is a binary object format; an LLM cannot manipulate its page tree or produce a valid PDF byte stream.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A pure-Python PDF library edits the page tree deterministically to merge/split/rotate while preserving content.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/py-pdf/pypdf (successor to PyPDF2), PyPI 'pypdf', BSD-3. Deterministic page operations.

candidates.intent: Extract the embedded text layer (and per-page text) from a digital PDF, preserving reading order where available.
candidates.input_contract: a PDF file/bytes (with a text layer)
candidates.output_contract: extracted text per page
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot read the binary content streams of a PDF; without extraction it has nothing to reason over.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic content-stream parsing pulls the exact embedded text and word/character positions.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/jsvine/pdfplumber, PyPI 'pdfplumber', MIT. Deterministic for digital PDFs; scanned PDFs need OCR (residual).

candidates.intent: Encode text/URL/data into a QR code and render it as an image or SVG.
candidates.input_contract: a string/bytes payload plus error-correction and size options
candidates.output_contract: a QR-code image (PNG/SVG) encoding the payload
candidates.gap_hypothesis: QR encoding applies precise Reed-Solomon error correction and module placement an LLM cannot compute.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic QR encoder produces a scannable, spec-correct code for any payload.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/lincolnloop/python-qrcode, PyPI 'qrcode', BSD-3. Deterministic encoding.

candidates.intent: Generate standard 1-D barcodes (EAN-13, Code128, UPC-A, etc.) as SVG or image with correct check digits.
candidates.input_contract: a barcode type plus the data payload
candidates.output_contract: a rendered barcode (SVG/PNG) with a valid check digit
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Barcode symbologies have exact module patterns and check-digit math an LLM cannot reproduce reliably.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic encoder computes check digits and renders spec-correct, scannable barcodes.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/WhyNotHugo/python-barcode, PyPI 'python-barcode', MIT. Deterministic, no external deps.

candidates.intent: Detect and decode QR codes and 1-D barcodes present in an image back to their payloads.
candidates.input_contract: an image file/bytes containing barcodes
candidates.output_contract: decoded payloads with type and bounding boxes
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Decoding a barcode from pixels requires precise signal processing; a text LLM cannot do it and a vision model is unreliable on dense codes.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A binding to the zbar engine deterministically locates and decodes barcodes with exact payloads.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/NaturalHistoryMuseum/pyzbar (zbar binding), PyPI 'pyzbar', MIT. Deterministic decode; coverage limited by image quality.

candidates.intent: Convert colors between representations (hex, RGB, HSL/HSV, CMYK, LAB) and compute color differences/contrast.
candidates.input_contract: a color value in a source space plus the target space
candidates.output_contract: the color in the target space (and optional contrast/distance)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Color-space conversions are exact matrix/curve transforms; an LLM approximates and drifts, breaking deterministic color math.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic conversion functions apply the exact color-space formulae reproducibly.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/vaab/colour, PyPI 'colour', BSD-2. Deterministic conversions.

candidates.intent: Compute the geodesic/great-circle distance and bearing between two latitude/longitude points.
candidates.input_contract: two (lat, lon) coordinate pairs plus an ellipsoid/model
candidates.output_contract: a distance (km/mi) and optional bearing
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot accurately compute geodesic distance (Vincenty/Karney) — it estimates and is wrong by kilometers.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Implements exact geodesic formulae deterministically for precise distances and bearings.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/geopy/geopy, PyPI 'geopy', MIT. The distance math is fully deterministic (geocoding/network parts excluded).

candidates.intent: Perform planar geometry operations and predicates — intersection, union, buffer, contains, distance, area — on points/lines/polygons.
candidates.input_contract: geometry objects (WKT/GeoJSON-like) plus an operation
candidates.output_contract: a resulting geometry or a boolean/measurement
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Computational geometry (point-in-polygon, intersections, buffers) is exact and an LLM cannot compute it reliably.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Bindings to the GEOS engine perform robust, deterministic geometric predicates and operations.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/shapely/shapely (GEOS binding), PyPI 'shapely', BSD-3. Deterministic geometry.

candidates.intent: Transform coordinates between coordinate reference systems / projections (e.g. WGS84 to UTM, EPSG codes).
candidates.input_contract: coordinates plus source and target CRS (EPSG/PROJ)
candidates.output_contract: coordinates in the target CRS
candidates.gap_hypothesis: CRS transformation requires the PROJ database and exact projection math an LLM does not have and cannot compute.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A PROJ binding applies authoritative, deterministic datum/projection transforms.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/pyproj4/pyproj (PROJ binding), PyPI 'pyproj', MIT. Deterministic transforms.

candidates.intent: Encode lat/lon into a geohash string and decode a geohash back to a bounding box / centroid.
candidates.input_contract: (lat, lon) + precision (encode) or a geohash string (decode)
candidates.output_contract: a geohash string, or a bounding box / centroid
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Geohash encoding interleaves bits with a precise base-32 scheme an LLM cannot reproduce exactly.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic geohash codec produces exact, reversible encodings.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/hkwi/python-geohash, PyPI 'python-geohash', Apache-2.0. Deterministic codec.

candidates.intent: Compute descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, stdev, quantiles, correlation) over numeric data.
candidates.input_contract: one or more numeric arrays/sequences
candidates.output_contract: the requested statistics as numbers
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM does mental arithmetic on arrays and is wrong/non-reproducible; statistics over real data must be exact.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Vectorized, numerically stable routines compute exact statistics deterministically at scale.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/numpy/numpy, PyPI 'numpy', BSD-3. Deterministic numeric computation.

candidates.intent: Run standard statistical tests (t-test, chi-square, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney, correlation tests) and return statistics and p-values.
candidates.input_contract: sample arrays plus the test to run
candidates.output_contract: a test statistic and p-value (and effect size where applicable)
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot compute correct test statistics or p-values from raw data — it fabricates plausible numbers.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Reference implementations of statistical tests return exact, reproducible statistics and p-values.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/scipy/scipy, PyPI 'scipy', BSD-3. Deterministic statistics.

candidates.intent: Compute a line/character diff between two texts and produce/apply patches (unified diff, opcodes).
candidates.input_contract: two text blocks (diff) or a text + patch (apply)
candidates.output_contract: a structured diff / unified-diff text, or the patched text
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM asked to diff two files invents changes, misaligns lines, and is not reproducible — diffs must be exact.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A deterministic longest-matching-block algorithm produces exact, reproducible diffs and opcodes.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: CPython stdlib difflib, PSF License. Deterministic diffing.

candidates.intent: Compute character-level diffs, do fuzzy match-location, and apply patches that tolerate slight target drift.
candidates.input_contract: two texts (diff), or a pattern + text (match), or text + patches (apply)
candidates.output_contract: diffs, a best match index, or patched text with applied-flags
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Robust fuzzy patching with location weighting is an exact algorithm; an LLM cannot reproduce its behavior deterministically.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Google's diff-match-patch applies the precise Myers-diff + fuzzy-match algorithms deterministically.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/google/diff-match-patch, Apache-2.0. Deterministic algorithm.

candidates.intent: Compute string-similarity metrics — Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, Hamming — and a similarity ratio.
candidates.input_contract: two strings plus the metric to compute
candidates.output_contract: a numeric distance or normalized similarity ratio
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM estimates edit distance instead of computing it, giving wrong, non-reproducible numbers unusable for dedupe thresholds.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: C-accelerated exact edit-distance routines return precise, reproducible distances and ratios.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/rapidfuzz/Levenshtein, PyPI 'Levenshtein', GPL-2.0 (note: copyleft). RapidFuzz (MIT) is the permissive alternative — see separate candidate.

candidates.intent: Perform fast fuzzy string matching and ranking (ratio, partial-ratio, token-sort) and extract best matches from a list.
candidates.input_contract: a query string plus a list of choices and a scorer
candidates.output_contract: ranked matches with similarity scores
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM cannot deterministically score and rank fuzzy matches across thousands of candidates; results vary and don't scale.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: A C++-accelerated library computes exact similarity scores and extracts top matches deterministically and fast.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz, PyPI 'RapidFuzz', MIT. Deterministic, permissive alternative to python-Levenshtein.

candidates.intent: Compute phonetic encodings (Soundex, Metaphone, NYSIIS) and string-distance metrics for name matching.
candidates.input_contract: a string (phonetic) or two strings (distance) plus the algorithm
candidates.output_contract: a phonetic code or a distance/similarity value
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Phonetic algorithms have exact rule tables an LLM does not reproduce; name-matching results would be inconsistent.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Deterministic implementations of the classic phonetic and distance algorithms give exact, reproducible codes.
candidates.verify_note: Verified: github.com/jamesturk/jellyfish, PyPI 'jellyfish', MIT. Deterministic.

candidates.intent: Convert Markdown source into HTML with configurable extensions (tables, fenced code, footnotes).
candidates.input_contract: Markdown text plus enabled extensions
candidates.output_contract: rendered HTML
candidates.gap_hypothesis: An LLM rendering Markdown to HTML is inconsistent on edge cases (nested lists, code fences) and not spec-stable.
